items.text: That "I want it" or "I can't stand it" may be the sound of a stored memory replaying on its own.
This urge isn't the real you. It's an old memory playing back. Try speaking to the replay.
When "it has to be this way" rings loud, that's a sign a memory is replaying.
Expectation and hurry are replays too. Wiping the screen won't stop it; the projector is inside.
If the same worry keeps returning, maybe the same film is running inside, not outside.
Asking "why?" over and over feeds the replay. You don't need the reason. You can just let it go.
The fixation isn't part of you. It's a memory you've been carrying.
Today's irritation may just be an old memory, stored long ago, taking its turn to play.
Noticing it's a replay is faster than thinking it through. Noticing is already half of letting go.
That unfilled feeling isn't a hole in the real you. It's the shape of a memory replaying.
The more we "know," the thicker the wall. Admitting "I don't know" opens a door.
Straining to stop the replay is a replay too. Relax, and offer one word.
It looks like their words moved you, but what moved was a memory inside you. You can release it without changing them.
The feeling aimed at them is a memory replaying inside you. The real you stands outside that replay.
Something is replaying in you, not in the person you're angry at. Say "thank you" to that.
That person may have just shown you where a memory lives in you. What's shown can be released.
"If only they would change" is reaching for the screen. The projector is on this side.
Your judgment of them is a label a memory stuck on. Release the label, and they look a little different.
If you keep stumbling on the same kind of person, maybe it's the same film replaying, not the same person.
You don't have to fix them. When the replay inside you settles, the temperature of the relationship changes too.
Wanting to blame is real. And it's also a memory replaying. You can hold both at once.
What looks like their not understanding may be your own "please understand me" memory replaying.
Peace doesn't start with them. It starts where the replay inside you goes quiet.
Their words may have been a button that started a replay in you. Say "thank you" to the button.
The voice saying "I'm no good" isn't you. It's a stored memory playing back.
Self-blame is a replay too. The real you is neither the one blaming nor the one being blamed.
A memory of shame is replaying right now. Say "I love you" to the replay.
Taking responsibility and blaming yourself are different. Taking it back returns the power to let go.
You are not the problem. A memory replaying inside you is wearing the shape of a problem.
"Do better" may be an old voice someone once used, replaying now. Not the real you speaking.
The gaze watching the you who couldn't do it is a memory too. Say "thank you" to the gaze.
Imperfection isn't a flaw. It's just memories not yet released.
When you're about to dislike yourself, remember: there's a quiet place inside you can return to.
Try saying "I don't know." Your verdict on yourself is one of the things you don't have to know.
The child inside is showing you an old hurt. Don't scold. Say "thank you for showing me."
Regret is an old film. If you notice it's replaying now, you can release it now.
What's happening now may be a memory replaying, not the real you. Offer it one word.
What appears outside is the shadow of a replay inside. You don't have to fight the shadow.
What you're aware of is only a small part of what's happening. You can let go without understanding it all.
Today's replay, released today. One "thank you" is enough.
One word before sleep. The rest can be left to tomorrow.
What you're seeing and hearing arrives through a filter of memory. Offer the filter one word, and what comes in arrives a little clearer.
The same view looks different depending on which memory is replaying. Before you look: thank you.
When you listen to someone, it may be your memory doing the listening. One word before you listen.
News and messages arrive through the filter of memory. Before you open them: I love you.
Nothing new can come in when an old film covers the entrance. Clear the entrance, often.
Release before the reaction, and the replay that would have played sometimes doesn't.
Everything you see and hear is a chance to let go. No special time is needed.
Just noticing that a filter is on changes what comes in, a little.
Everything you'll see and hear today passes through a filter of memory. One word to the filter, this morning.
(bell) Which filter are you looking through right now? One "thank you."
Don't place the cause outside. Take it 100% as a replay inside you. That isn't blame — it's taking back the power to let go.
You pick it up yourself, and you set it down yourself. No one can do it for you — so there's no one to blame.
Not even an inch of the problem is outside. It's all on this side — which isn't despair; it means all of it can be released from here.
Step down from the victim's seat, and the maker's seat is open.
There's exactly one way the world changes without changing them: taking on the replay inside you.
To take 100% is to be 100% free.
